conviction_note: No company-level unpriced number found. The evidence is a set of small, mostly offsetting proxies: a sharp Q3 rate shock (10y +80bp to 5.3%, a Fed hike on 9/16, 30y mortgage at 7.4%) that puts the Q4 NIM guide of 2.80% and tangible book at risk, and CRE nonaccrual upticks at peers, against a New England peer (INDB) that beat and rose 4.85% and a short base that grew to 11.5 days to cover. abs_move 6.5 sits above the 3.56 median because the last three prints moved 8-17%, and p_up 47 carries the slight negative lean. The findings sum (-0.7) and the scaled number (-0.39) agree in sign and are both small.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus $0.87 and revenue $62.5M (Benzinga, updated 2026-10-13, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WASH/earnings-forecasts, read via search snippet), with $0.86 average, range $0.84-0.88, from 3 analysts on Tickflow (https://tickflow.io/stock/WASH/forecast, snippet). The two sources roughly agree. Company guide from the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15265414580347904): Q3 NIM about 2.75%, Q4 about 2.80%, Q3 expenses up about $1M to just under $39M, mid single-digit loan growth for 2026, 2026 tax rate about 21.5%. My own bottom-up read off that guide (NIM 2.75% on about $6.2B of earning assets gives NII of about $42.6M, with fees around $18.5M) lands near $0.85-0.86, slightly under the bar.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/wash/shortinterest, read 2026-10-19): 1,381,186 shares on the 2026-09-30 settlement, 11.52 days to cover. That is about 7.2% of 19.07M shares outstanding, up from 1,179,138 shares and 7.87 days on 2026-07-15. The 10-15 settlement is not yet published. The short is rising and fairly crowded for a thin name (20-day average volume about 113k), which argues for shrinking the negatives. The baseline has no usable option chain (ATM not two-sided, total open interest 39, put/call open interest 0.15), so there is no skew. Unusual Whales shows a priced move of ±9.61% as of 2026-10-19 (https://unusualwhales.com/stock/WASH/earnings), but that is almost certainly off wide, untraded quotes and is not a usable anchor. Run-up: -6.23% over 20 days, -1.5% over 5 days, 8.8% below the 52-week high and 42% above the 52-week low (set after the April -16.9% reaction).

findings.finding: Rates rose sharply through Q3 2026, and that puts management's Q4 NIM guide of about 2.80% (given 2026-07-21) at risk on this print's outlook. The Fed raised to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, its first hike since 2023, with the median dot implying one more by year-end. The 10-year went from about 4.5% at 6/30 to 5.3% at 9/30. WASH funds with $456M of FHLB advances and CDs, and on the Q2 call management said CDs had 'a little bit left to go' repricing DOWN and that earlier hopes for rate cuts had not materialised. If the Q4 2.80% is held or raised, this is a positive (the steeper curve helps new production); if it is cut, it is the main negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-20): a beat plus 'confidence in the outlook' and the NIM guide bought +8.15%. Q1 2026: an earnings miss on credit cost -16.9%. This stock trades the print hard in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: The macro move is public, but whether WASH re-affirms or cuts its specific 2.80% Q4 NIM guide is not knowable before the call. If the market had priced a guide cut, the stock would trade well below the July levels and the $38 consensus target. Instead it is only 6% off its 20-day high, and the consensus of $0.87 is above Q2's $0.83, so the street is still modelling NIM expansion.
findings.independence: Rate path: CNBC https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-rate-decision-september-2026.html. 10y at 5.3% on 9/30: First Citizens Q3 review https://www.firstcitizens.com/content/dam/firstcitizens/pdfs/wealth/market-outlook/2026/q3-2026-quarterly-market-review.pdf. Peer funding: M&T attributed its Q3 NIM decline partly to higher funding costs (https://newsroom.mtb.com/2026-10-16-M-T-Bank-Corporation-NYSE-MTB-announces-third-quarter-2026-results). Counter-evidence: INDB's NIM rose 4bp and Regions' deposit cost was flat. This is a macro-to-company proxy; the company has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: Q3's rate rise will mark down WASH's AFS book and shrink book value and TBV in the release. At 6/30/2026, AFS securities had an amortized cost of $982.0M against a fair value of $885.3M, with $100.0M of gross unrealized losses and AOCI of -$77.4M. A roughly 70-80bp rise in the intermediate curve over Q3 implies a further pre-tax mark of about $30-45M, or about $1.2-1.8 per share after tax against a Q2 BVPS of $29.02. That is roughly a 4-6% drop in book. CET1 is unaffected (AOCI opt-out).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior WASH print has turned on an AOCI move that I can source. The last large rate-driven book declines were in 2022-23, outside the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Anyone with the 10-Q and the curve can compute this, so it is mostly priced; the -6.2% 20-day drift is consistent with it. What is left is the headline TBV decline in the release, read by holders who track price/TBV.
findings.independence: The rate move rests on the same series as the first finding (First Citizens Q3 review). This is the balance-sheet effect of that same macro fact, not a second fact: it lands on book value, not on NIM.

findings.finding: The Q3 mortgage environment worsened late in the quarter. The Freddie Mac 30-year rate was 6.66-6.69% in August, then rose to 6.95% on 9/17, 7.03% on 9/24 and 7.28% on 10/1. WASH's Q2 mortgage banking revenue was $3.5M (up 14% QoQ, originations $216M up 39%) with a $121M pipeline at 6/30. Q3 sales volume probably held through August, but the pipeline and Q4 commentary weaken.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Mortgage banking is about 6% of revenue and has never been the cited driver of a WASH reaction in the sources I found.
findings.why_not_priced: Small line; most of the rise came in the last two weeks of the quarter, so the effect is mostly a Q4 one and analysts may have left Q3 mortgage flat.
findings.independence: Q2 mortgage figures: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000737468/000073746826000109/exhibit9912026q2.htm. The rate series is a proxy; the company has not confirmed any effect.

findings.finding: The terminated cash-flow-hedge amortization ended on 1 May 2026. Q2 carried two months of the benefit ($1.4M, 9bp of NIM); Q3 carries a full three months, about $0.7M more NII (about 4bp) per management. The release calls it a permanent improvement to run-rate earnings. This sits inside the Q3 2.75% NIM guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 NIM step-up of 10bp, mostly this item, came with a +8.15% reaction, although that print also beat on credit and EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: It is guided, so it is mostly priced. It is filed because it mechanically supports the Q3 NIM number and helps the 2.75% hold against funding pressure.
findings.independence: The Q2 call transcript gives the same figure (https://www.webull.com/news/15265414580347904), so it is the same company source and counts once.

findings.finding: Peer read-through, positive: Independent Bank Corp (Rockland Trust), the largest Massachusetts-based peer in WASH's southern New England footprint, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-15. EPS was $1.90 against a Zacks average of $1.84, NIM 3.89% (+4bp QoQ), loans +0.9%, deposits +0.7%, a $57.4M buyback, and the shares rose 4.85% the next day. That is a clean regional print after WASH last spoke on 2026-07-21.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced history of WASH trading on INDB's print; the two share deposit and CRE markets in MA/RI.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: WASH did not visibly re-rate after it (5-day run-up -1.5%). If the market had read INDB through to WASH, the 5-day run-up would be positive rather than drifting lower.
findings.independence: INDB results: https://finviz.com/news/403305/independent-bank-corp-reports-third-quarter-net-income-of-897-million. Regions' deposit cost was flat at 1.17% vs 1.18% (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026). INDB's business mix differs: its NIM is about 115bp higher and it has no big wealth arm.

findings.finding: Peer read-through, negative on credit: Q3 2026 releases on 2026-10-16 show CRE nonaccruals rising at Northeast lenders. NB Bancorp (Greater Boston) had nonperforming loans up 30.4% to $36.1M (0.53% of loans vs 0.43%), partly on a CRE loan placed on nonaccrual, and net charge-offs of 0.31% vs 0.07%. M&T's net charge-offs rose to 0.35% from 0.23%. WASH's own open items: a $28.9M office loan 90+ days past due and on nonaccrual, office nonaccruals of $28.9M against $35.0M classified office, and a $3.8M Class B special-mention office loan that matured in Q3. Q1's specific reserve build on two office loans cost -16.9% when it landed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit is the line this stock trades on: Q1 2026 (nonaccruals 0.25% to 0.81%, $4.0M provision) gave -16.9%. Q2 (nonaccruals edged down to 0.78%, provision $1.6M) gave +8.15%.
findings.why_not_priced: The WASH-specific outcome (a charge-off or resolution on the $28.9M loan, and the $3.8M maturity) is not public. The 20-day -6.2% and the rising short interest suggest some of this worry is in the price; a market sure of a second credit hit would show a deeper drawdown toward the April $30 level.
findings.independence: WASH office book detail: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000737468/000073746826000109/exhibit9912026q2.htm and https://www.webull.com/news/15265414580347904. M&T: https://newsroom.mtb.com/2026-10-16-M-T-Bank-Corporation-NYSE-MTB-announces-third-quarter-2026-results. The peers are proxies; INDB showed no reported credit issue.

findings.finding: Short interest built steadily into the print: 1,179,138 shares on the 7/15 settlement became 1,407,333 on 8/31 and 1,381,186 on 9/30, which is 11.52 days to cover on about 113k shares a day of volume (about 7.2% of shares outstanding). With no listed options worth trading, the short is the main positioning. A clean credit quarter forces covering into a thin tape; the Q2 +8.15% came off a smaller short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 +8.15% on a beat with about 1.2M shares short; Q4 2025 +12.69%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is asymmetric rather than priced. 11.5 days to cover means that if the credit line comes back clean, the shorts cannot exit without lifting the price.
findings.independence: Benzinga showed 6.3% short float in August (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WASH/short-interest, snippet). Same FINRA data underneath.

findings.finding: Bottom-up check of the bar: guided Q3 NIM of 2.75% on about $6.2B of average earning assets (Q2 NII $41.8M at 2.73% implies about $6.12B) gives NII of about $42.6M. Fees: wealth about $11.0M (Q2's $11.2M included seasonal tax-servicing fees; S&P +2.3% in Q3 helps asset-based fees), mortgage about $3.0-3.5M, other about $4M, so fees are about $18.5M. Revenue comes to about $61M against a $62.5M consensus. With expenses just under $39M (guided), a provision of about $1.5M and a 21.5% tax rate, EPS is about $0.85-0.86 against the $0.86-0.87 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: a miss on EPS ($0.66) and revenue ($57.8M) gave -16.9%, though credit drove it. Q2: a beat of $0.83 against $0.77-0.79 gave +8.15%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $0.87 sits above a straight read of the company's own NIM and expense guide. If analysts had marked fees down for the end of the tax season and the late-quarter mortgage slowdown, revenue consensus would be closer to $61M. This is my arithmetic, not a document, and the revenue definitions may differ.
findings.independence: Consensus figures: Benzinga and Tickflow snippets (see bar). Q2 base: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000737468/000073746826000109/exhibit9912026q2.htm. This shares the guide document with the hedge finding; the hedge benefit is already inside the 2.75%, so it is not counted twice.

findings.finding: Wealth AUA ended Q2 at a record $7.92B (+5.6% QoQ, +10.2% YoY). The S&P 500 rose 2.3% in Q3 with a -0.35% September, while long bonds sold off. Asset-based fees should be flat to slightly up, with the seasonal Q2 tax-servicing fees falling away.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Wealth has not been the cited driver of a WASH reaction in the sources found.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and largely predictable; filed for completeness. The bond sell-off partly offsets the equity gain in balanced client portfolios.
findings.independence: AUA figure from the Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000737468/000073746826000109/exhibit9912026q2.htm. The market level is a proxy.

findings.finding: A 2026 share repurchase program has run since 2026-05-16 (10-Q glossary). No treasury purchases were made in H1 2026, and the Q2 release does not mention buybacks. The stock fell 6% into the print with CET1 at 11.89%, so either a first use in Q3 or an announced intent would be a modest positive. INDB bought back $57.4M in Q3.
findings.why_not_priced: Not mentioned on the Q2 call or in the release, so it is not in previews.

findings.why_not_priced: Public for months; filed at 0 because the buys and the later sale offset.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The slight negative lean agrees with the -6.2% 20-day drift and the rising short interest, so it is probably partly priced. The crowded short (11.5 days to cover) cuts against it, which is why the negatives are small and p_up is only 3 points under 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short, 11.5 days to cover): rate/NIM-guide finding shrunk from -1.0 to -0.8 and peer-credit finding from -0.8 to -0.6
Rule 2 (one-off below operating income with no path to the guide): AOCI/TBV finding shrunk from -0.3 to -0.2
Rule 5 (my own arithmetic is inference, not a document): bottom-up bar check shrunk from -0.4 to -0.3
Rule 8 and the pessimism artefact: abs_move raised from 6.0 to 6.5 (the last three prints moved 8-17%) and p_up moved from 46 to 47
Rule 6: bar sourced to two roughly agreeing estimates ($0.87 Benzinga, $0.86 Tickflow) plus the company NIM and expense guide, so no cap applied
